free_tier.stated: Developer key, free: up to 500 calls a day and 1 call a second, with article text, over 1,900,000 pieces of content.
free_tier.notes: The 500 a day is per API key and expires at the close of each day. One key is issued for each website that uses the content. The archive dates back to 1999. A commercial key has a custom throttle and quota, priced by usage. The access page listed 12 calls a second and 5,000 calls a day before a later change to 1 and 500.

per_object_cap.notes: Paging by page number stops at a depth of several thousand results; deeper paging goes through the content /next endpoint.

retention.stated: content held must be replaced by re-requesting it, or deleted, at least every 24 hours

interface_detail: REST over HTTPS at content.guardianapis.com (/search, /tags, /sections, /editions and single items); the key goes in the api-key parameter
chaining: Full article text in the answer, within 500 calls a day; any held copy is refreshed or dropped within 24 hours.

limits.value: 500 calls a day per developer key
1 call a second per developer key (60 calls a minute)
content held must be replaced or deleted at least every 24 hours

binding_note: 500 calls a day is met first; the 24-hour hold limit governs any local copy.

identity_cost.detail: The developer-key form asks for a name, an email entered twice, an educational institution or company name, a reason (student project, academic research, non-commercial app development, other), a short description of use, whether content will be displayed, a product name, optional product and company URLs, and acceptance of the terms; a Google reCAPTCHA is shown when Register is pressed, and the key is sent to the email. The institution or company name is a required free-text field of at most 200 characters with no list or pattern. No card or phone field. The Open Platform front page offers the developer key as free instant access, the key tool's repository describes self-serve key management, and the commercial key is a request that the team follows up. Posts on the vendor's support forum describe an email with a verification link sent after the form, a link that can be invalid or expired, a refusal to register again with an address already in use, and a key registered to a free-mail address; a course page describes a confirmation email followed by a second email with the key. Whether the institution or company name is checked after the form is sent is unverified: behind a sign-up. How soon the key email arrives is unverified: behind a sign-up.

reliability_note: Keys can be cancelled or suspended at any time without notice. A call with the demo key test answered HTTP 401 on 2026-10-31.
confidence_note: Quota, rate, hold limit and form fields are read from first-party pages, and staff replies on the vendor's support forum give the daily and per-minute limits of a developer key; a keyless call answered HTTP 401 'No API key found in request' and the demo key test answered HTTP 401 'Unauthorized', so no call returned content and the enforced rate is unmeasured. Key issuance rests on the form and on user posts, not on a completed registration. A call with an issued key, reading its rate-limit response headers, would move the limits to measured.
